Make yourself at home

Up and running
in a few steps

Start with the tools you already use. Camp reads their local sessions and continues through their own command-line clients.

  1. Bring your tools

    Install Codex CLI, Claude Code, or both, and sign in. You’ll also need Python 3.11 or newer. A source build needs Apple’s Xcode Command Line Tools.

  2. Build your camp

    Clone the public repository and run the local build. It creates the app in the build folder.

    git clone https://github.com/teslashibe/capybara-camp.git
cd capybara-camp
./build.sh
open "build/Capybara Camp.app"

    Missing Apple’s build tools? Run xcode-select --install first.

  3. Bring your sessions to camp

    Open the app and let the first import finish. Add other profile folders in Manage sources. Open a card to chat, then send with ⌘ Return. During a reply, use the same shortcut to steer, or ⌘ ⇧ Return to queue.

Using the download? The universal ZIP includes both Mac architectures. Extract it and move Capybara Camp.app to Applications. The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, so macOS may block it. Read Apple’s guidance or use the source build above. Python and the provider CLIs are still required. A SHA-256 checksum is included with the release.

Local sessions, familiar logins

Credentials stay with the provider CLI. Camp stores its board, profile paths, model settings and queued prompts locally. Sending a message still contacts the selected provider through its CLI.

New sessions are discovered automatically. An open transcript follows saved file changes immediately, while Camp-started replies stream directly.

A deliberately small first release

This is a chat-only preview: Camp-started turns have tools, hooks and MCP servers disabled. Close a session in the other app before sending into it from Camp.

Account management, usage dashboards, automatic account switching and provider-native dictation are not included yet. External terminal chats update as their CLI saves text; Camp does not attach to their live token stream.
